Symbols:
  \phi: Fraction of reduced centers on the catalyst surface. [-] (computed)
  \gamma^{*}: Contact-surface free-energy quantity in the numerator of the ratio γ*/γ0. (computed)
  \gamma_{0}: Reference contact-surface free-energy quantity in the ratio γ*/γ0. (computed)
  K_{1}: Equilibrium constant for reaction 1. [-] (computed)
  K_{2}: Equilibrium constant for reaction 2. [-] (computed)
  p_{H_2}: Partial pressure of hydrogen. (variable)
  p_{CO}: Partial pressure of CO. (variable)
  p_{H_2O}: Partial pressure of water used in the model equations. [bar] (variable)
  p_{CO_2}: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide used in the model equations. [bar] (variable)
  k_{1}: Kinetic rate constant for CO hydrogenation. (parameter)
  \Delta G_{1}: Gibbs free-energy change associated with equilibrium constant K₁. [J mol^-1] (parameter)
  R: Gas constant. [J mol^-1 K^-1] (parameter)
  T: Temperature. [K] (variable)
  k_{2}: Rate constant in the CO₂ reaction-rate expression. (parameter)
  \Delta G_{2}: Gibbs free-energy change associated with equilibrium constant K₂. [J mol^-1] (parameter)
  y_{H_2}: Gas-phase fraction of hydrogen. [-] (variable)
  y_{H_2O}: Gas-phase fraction of water. [-] (variable)
  y_{CO}: Gas-phase fraction of carbon monoxide. [-] (variable)
  y_{CO_2}: Gas-phase fraction of carbon dioxide. [-] (variable)
  y_{i}: Mole fraction of component i. [-] (computed)
  Z: Compressibility factor. [-] (parameter)
  \tau: Hold-up time. [s] (variable)
  y_{i,0}: Mole fraction of component i at input. [-] (variable)
  K: Factor normalizing the reaction-rate contribution in the mole-fraction balance. (parameter)
  \nu_{ij}: Stoichiometric coefficient of component i in reaction j. [-] (parameter)
  r_{j}: Rate of reaction j. (variable)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Catalyst deactivation neglected; only reactions (1)-(3) considered.
  - Langmuir‑Hinshelwood mechanism with adsorption, surface reaction, desorption.
  - Oxidized centers (⊙) are active for CO hydrogenation.
  - Reduced centers (∗) are active for CO₂ hydrogenation.
  - Total numbers of oxidized, reduced and hydrogen centers are constant.
  - Fast steps are at quasi‑equilibrium.
  - Quasi‑equilibrium assumption for fast adsorption/desorption steps.
  - Lumped kinetics for reactions (1)-(3).
  - Two alternatives for φ: quasistatic (Eq.22) or dynamic (Eq.28).
